case_reviews.model_answer:
Totally understandable — Tokyo looks intimidating on the map, but honestly it's one of the easiest big cities to get around. You already have the hardest part sorted: your Suica.

A few things that'll make it feel calmer:

- **Trust your Suica.** Tap in and out at the gates, and it covers JR, metro, and buses. Top up at any ticket machine with cash. No PIN, no faff.
- **Google Maps is your best friend.** It'll tell you the exact platform, which train car to board (handy for getting near the exits), and which station exit to leave from. Exit numbers matter — Shinjuku has dozens of exits, so follow the number, not your instincts.
- **Station signs are bilingual**, and every station has a number code. Even with zero Japanese, you can match characters on the platform signs to what the map shows.
- **Avoid rush hour if you can** (roughly 7:30–9:30am and 5–7pm). Packed but fine — you'll survive, it's just less fun.
- **Last trains run around midnight.** If you're out late, check the last train time before you commit, or just take a taxi. Pricey (that Shinjuku–Tsukiji run would set you back ¥4,000–5,000), but a good fallback.
- **You're in a great base.** Shinjuku is a major hub, so almost everywhere is one transfer at most. Even Tsukiji is just Yamanote Line to Shimbashi, then Ginza Line — about half an hour.

The one tip I'd really emphasize: if you ever get turned around, walk to the nearest station and ask staff. They're used to tourists, and most can understand enough English to point you the right way.

By day two it'll feel completely normal, I promise.
